content: We also measure the performance of Multitask Question Answering Network (MQAN) BIBREF18 a QA model trained by the authors on the Decathlon multitask challenge. Since MQAN was not trained to produce the output sequence in our MR tags, it would not be fair to compute ROUGE scores. Instead, we randomly sample the MQAN's predictions from the 10% test dataset and qualitatively evaluate it. From the evaluations, we find that MQAN can not distinguish between frequency and dosage, and mixed the answers. MQAN correctly predicted the dosage for 29.73% and frequency for 24.24% percent of the medications compared to 84.12% and 76.34% for the encoder pretrained BERT QA PGNet model trained on our dataset. This could be because of the difference in the training dataset, domain and the tasks in the Decathlon challenge compared to ours.
